package_only_contract: Accept an explicit existing result directory and a fresh destination outside the campaign and source result tree; reject existing destination and path overlap before mutation.

Read existing FINAL_STATUS.json first and validate its existing wrapper schema: JSON object, recognized status string, solver_runs=0 and scientific_admission=NOT_ISSUED; do not invent replacement science fields. Preserve it byte-for-byte in recovered evidence; absent, malformed, unrecognized or contradictory science status remains UNKNOWN/HOLD and never becomes SUCCESS from archive success.

Preserve original result directory entirely, including partial ZIP. Copy arbitrary original report payload files, including JSON/PNG/logs, to fresh destination without rewriting scientific status, plots, receipts or logs. Exclude the old report ZIP from the new archive; retain its original bytes on disk and identify that source in recovery receipt.

Build a new archive from the preserved payload plus corrected runnable wrapper and unchanged renderer dependencies; external raw scientific inputs remain external and indexed. Verify archive CRC and representative payload readback.

Do not invoke inspect-based readiness gating, bind, render, subprocess solver, watcher, retries, SSH, or campaign modification in package-only recovery. Packaging preserved results is permitted after the original render deadline because it performs no rendering or scientific computation.

Record original scientific_status and distinct packaging_status in stdout/recovery receipt. Packaging errors must retain the known original science status, error and recoverable paths; never report an undifferentiated REQUEST_FAILED as the sole outcome. Define package-only exit code explicitly as packaging operation outcome, if using zero for a packaged failed scientific result; stdout and prompt must state that zero is not scientific success.

Apply separate packaging error reporting to the original render command too: an archive failure after successful or failed rendering must not erase its already-written result status. Retain failure exit code when packaging fails.
ncp_prompt_contract: User action is only copy/paste into NCP Codex. The prompt instructs Codex itself to fetch the repaired bundle from a concrete published immutable revision/URL, verify its stated identity and extract it into a fresh path; no user download, shell command, token disclosure or manual file transfer.

Locate /root/rei-post-*/results and other explicitly known wrapper output paths using a bounded one-shot filesystem search. Inspect candidate FINAL_STATUS, render receipt and logs before deciding recovery; do not guess success or pick an ambiguous result silently.

For existing outputs, execute package-only recovery once into a fresh directory and report original science/render status, packaging outcome, preserved source and recovered artifact paths. This recovery never rerenders existing outputs.

If original render failed, classify the actual error from status/receipt/logs before proposing any later rerender. This contract does not authorize a blind rerender. If no result is found or status is uninterpretable, preserve evidence and report the specific unresolved state.

Any separately justified later render remains subject to the original finite shared bind+render budget, 8GiB address-space cap and absolute deadline; do not reset elapsed allowance, epoch or deadline. Expired or unprovable remaining render budget stops rendering.

limits.review: One implementation/verification pass and one independent scoped C9 pass; one targeted authorized repair if needed; no review recursion

acceptance: Synthetic pre-1980 archived files reproduce the old failure and package successfully with corrected metadata; input/result bytes and filesystem mtimes are unchanged.
Package-only recovery preserves a prior SUCCESS status and its payload, performs zero bind/render/subprocess calls, leaves original partial ZIP unchanged, and succeeds even after render deadline.
Prior failed/unknown science remains failed/unknown after successful packaging; injected packaging failure reports both dimensions without destroying evidence.
Fresh-destination/path-overlap guard prevents overwriting existing output; recovered ZIP CRC and expected runnable dependencies pass.

Reuse established 28 physics checks, 3 renderer CLI checks and 8 prior wrapper checks. Run new focused recovery regressions and only directly affected prior packaging/CLI checks when a concrete changed dependency warrants them; no automatic full-suite replay. Do not restart full Q512/Q1024 runs.

Pinned self-running prompt has concrete fetch identity and zero user-operated download/command steps; locally verified delivery must not claim NCP execution or scientific success that was not observed.
transition: Targeted checks PASS -> build/publish the authorized pinned recovery bundle -> hand user one executable Codex prompt. Existing-result recovery success -> report recovered archive and unchanged scientific status; no new scientific admission gate or numerical campaign.
